Fixr, by contrast, scales perfectly linearly (80 sq ft at $160–$400 = the same $2–$5/sq ft as 400 sq ft), which is almost certainly a calculator artifact and understates small-job totals.

anchors.conflicts: Two clusters that differ by ~4x on the low end, and they are not reconcilable by averaging. (1) Lead-gen marketplaces (Angi, HomeAdvisor, Thumbtack) publish $0.10-$0.50/sq ft, and their whole-job averages back that up: $311 national average / 2,000 sq ft = $0.16/sq ft. The likely cause is denominator, not real price disagreement: marketplace figures divide by the home's floor area (2,000 sq ft house), while contractor figures divide by actual cleaned surface area (siding elevation, deck boards, driveway slab), which for a 2,000 sq ft home is roughly 1,200-1,600 sq ft of wall plus a 600 sq ft driveway. Treat the $0.10-$0.20 band as house-footprint pricing and $0.35-$0.55 as true cleaned-surface pricing. Second, real disagreement by surface: hard flatwork (concrete driveway, sidewalk) is $0.20-$0.40 everywhere, while wood decks, fences, and painted siding needing soft-wash chemicals run $0.40-$0.80 — HomeGuide is explicit about this split, Angi and HomeAdvisor flatten it into one range.
